content:
{
  "root_cause": "Focus does not move into the drawer when opened via keyboard because the drawer's show method relies on the browser's automatic focus shift, which may not have completed when the test assertions run immediately after the click event listener returns.",
  "repair_strategy": "Override _showElement in the Drawer class to call the parent implementation and then explicitly move focus to the first focusable element inside the drawer (e.g., the close button), ensuring focus is transferred synchronously when the drawer opens.",
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "When the user opens the filters drawer with Enter, focus will move to the close button (or first focusable element). Subsequent Tab navigation will reach the In stock checkbox, then the Waterproof checkbox, and finally the Apply button, allowing keyboard-only operation to apply a filter and see the results update.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Overriding _showElement could interfere with any custom focus logic in subclasses, but Drawer has no known subclasses.",
    "If no focusable element is found, focus will remain unchanged, which is safe.",
    "Calling focus() on an already focused element is harmless and does not cause side effects."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "After pressing Enter on #filters-open, focus should be on #filters-close.",
    "Pressing Tab should move focus to #in-stock.",
    "Pressing Space should toggle the In stock checkbox.",
    "Pressing Tab twice should move focus to #apply.",
    "Pressing Enter on #apply should update #applied text to \"in\".",
    "Pressing Escape should close the drawer and return focus to #filters-open."
  ]
}
